title: MAPLE: Semi-Supervised Learning with Multi-Alignment and Pseudo-Learning

problem.claim: Learning from multiple data sources faces a substantial distribution gap between the target data and other sources, referred to as hybrid shift.

gap.claim: Existing methods tend to address the problem by manually annotating more data, whereas labor-free learning from multiple sources is not addressed by those methods.

contributions.claim: MAPLE is a method for learning deep models from multiple sources in a labor-free fashion.
MAPLE uses multiple discriminators in a multi-alignment module to align different data distributions through an adversarial process.
MAPLE introduces a semi-supervised learning manner to further improve the utility of the method.

stated_novelty.claim: The authors distinguish MAPLE as unlike previous methods and describe its semi-supervised learning manner as novel.

author_reported_evidence.claim: The authors report extensive evaluations on four benchmarks.
The authors report that MAPLE achieves state-of-the-art performance and outperforms existing methods by an obvious margin.

narrative_sequence.summary: Data augmentation has improved the training of high-accuracy deep networks, and recent work mines generalized knowledge from multiple sources.
Multiple-source learning introduces a large distribution gap between target data and other sources, while existing methods tend to require more manual annotation.
The paper proposes MAPLE for labor-free multi-source learning, using adversarial multi-alignment and semi-supervised learning.
The authors report effectiveness, state-of-the-art performance, and an obvious margin over existing methods across four benchmarks.

source_observation.claim: The method aligns multiple data distributions with multiple discriminators through an adversarial process.

interpretation.claim: When several source distributions differ from the target, alignment may need to model multiple distribution relationships rather than rely on a single alignment mechanism.

application.claim: Consider multi-discriminator adversarial alignment when building learning systems that combine heterogeneous data sources.

exception.claim: The abstract does not establish when multi-alignment is preferable to other distribution-alignment strategies.

unknowns: The abstract does not specify the four benchmarks, datasets, baselines, metrics, or numerical results.
The abstract does not explain the pseudo-learning procedure or its relationship to the semi-supervised component.
The abstract does not describe the data-source assumptions, annotation requirements, or computational costs.
